# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes the USDA final rule "Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks" (7 CFR part 2100), published as Federal Register document 2026-13092 on June 29, 2026, and effective July 29, 2026. The rule finalizes the USDA Feedstock Carbon Intensity Calculator (USDA FD-CIC), which quantifies, reports on, and verifies greenhouse gas reduction benefits from low-carbon agricultural practices used to produce biofuel feedstock crops. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The rule "supports the quantification, reporting, and verification of greenhouse gas (GHG) reduction benefits resulting from implementation of low-carbon practices in the production of commodities that are used as biofuel feedstocks in the context of environmental services markets." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.* It applies directly to farm producers of covered feedstock crops (field corn, soybeans, sorghum, spring canola) and to the first point of aggregation and intermediary entities handling reduced-carbon-intensity (reduced-CI) crop. For workspaces that arrange transport or forwarding for agricultural biofuel feedstocks, or that serve clients participating in reduced-CI feedstock or sustainable aviation fuel supply chains, this rule sets the federal documentation and carbon-intensity attestation regime those upstream counterparties must meet. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace itself, as a freight forwarder rather than a farm producer, aggregator, or intermediary entity, falls within any duty-holder class this rule defines.

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** Assess whether any current or prospective client shipping biofuel feedstock crops or reduced-CI processed product relies on USDA FD-CIC certification, since the rule "specifically applies to the production of low- carbon biofuel feedstocks for liquid transportation fuels, which presents a clear environmental services market." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.* *Operational implication:* a forwarder handling reduced-CI feedstock cargo may be asked by shippers to confirm chain-of-custody documentation aligns with the attestation records this rule requires further upstream, even though the forwarder itself is not a named duty-holder in the text. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The rule's obligations attach to farm producers, the first point of aggregation, and intermediary entities in the reduced-CI feedstock supply chain, not to carriers or forwarders. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any workspace activity (e.g., commissioning aggregation, warehousing, or onward distribution of reduced-CI feedstock crop on behalf of a client) brings the workspace within the "first point of aggregation" or "intermediary entities" language the rule uses for its attestation and recordkeeping duties. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# Substantive Requirements

**Carbon-intensity quantification and attestation.** Farm producers document field- or management-unit-level carbon intensity using USDA FD-CIC, which "estimates feedstock CIs based on user location, user supplied nutrient management information, and, if applicable, the impact of one or more low-carbon practices." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

**Recordkeeping and attestation under penalty of perjury.** The Biofuel Feedstock Report submitted by farm producers, and the attestations required of the first point of aggregation and intermediary entities, must be signed under penalty of perjury: the report must "begin with a statement that the undersigned farm producer certifies the following under penalties of perjury." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.* *Operational implication:* this is a federal false-statement liability mechanism, not a stated civil fine amount; a workspace advising a client on documentation integrity for reduced-CI cargo should treat the attestation as carrying personal legal exposure for the signer, distinct from any commercial penalty. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

**Third-party verification.** Entities "participating in multiple sustainability certification programs must now provide a third-party verifier with documentation related to their participation in those programs... in order to ensure that environmental benefits (i.e., GHG emissions reductions) are not accounted for in multiple programs." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

**Record retention.** Nutrient-management records supporting a claimed low-carbon practice "must be kept for 5 years." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

The rule does not establish a jurisdictional or producer registration scheme; it operates through the Biofuel Feedstock Report and third-party verification process described above rather than a standing agency registration. *Specific registration or filing deadline not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-12.*

# Operational System Requirements

For workspaces whose clients are farm producers, aggregators, or intermediary entities in the reduced-CI feedstock chain: (1) confirm the client's Biofuel Feedstock Report and supporting nutrient-management and manure-application records are retained for the 5-year window this rule sets, and (2) confirm any third-party verifier engagement covers all sustainability certification programs the client participates in, to avoid double-counted GHG benefit claims. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.* *Operational implication:* neither requirement creates a direct forwarding-side system build, since the recordkeeping duty sits with the producer, aggregator, or intermediary, not the carrier or forwarder. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- July 29, 2026: rule effective ("DATES: Effective date: July 29, 2026."). In force as of 2026-09-12. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*
- The interim rule preceding this final rule took public comment for 60 days, ending March 18, 2025, and USDA received 114 comments before finalizing the changes reflected in this rule. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# Sources

- Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register document 2026-13092, June 29 2026 (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks

entries.body:
# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes an EPA final rule (40 CFR part 63, Federal Register document 2026-12424, June 22, 2026) that implements a Congressional Review Act (CRA) disapproval of the 2024 amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAP) for Rubber Tire Manufacturing. "Under the joint resolution and by operation of the CRA, the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule has no legal force or effect, and the EPA thus is taking this final action to remove the provisions finalized in that rule." *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

"On March 5, 2025, the United States House of Representatives passed a joint resolution, H.J. Res. 61, disapproving the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule under the CRA (5 U.S.C. 801 et seq.). The United States Senate passed H.J. Res. 61 on May 6, 2025, and President Donald J. Trump signed it into law as Public Law 119-14 on May 23, 2025." *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.* The action "removes the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule's changes to 40 CFR part 63, subpart XXXX, and reverts to the regulatory text in effect immediately prior to the effective date of the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule," i.e., the 2020 Rubber Tire Rule. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.* The subpart applies to "any source that owns or operate a rubber tire manufacturing facility that is located at, or is a part of, a major source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions." *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.* For workspaces that forward cargo for, or serve, rubber tire manufacturers or rubber processing facilities in the United States, this reversion sets the currently binding federal emissions-control baseline those manufacturing clients operate under.

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** Confirm with any client that is a rubber tire or rubber processing manufacturer which emission-limitation regime it is currently operating under, since the "first-time air emissions standards for the rubber processing subcategory" introduced by the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule "has no legal force or effect" and the facility instead reverts to the 2020 Rubber Tire Rule's existing-source and new-source limitations. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.* *Operational implication:* a rubber processing subcategory facility that had begun building toward the 2024 standard's first-time limits no longer has a federal compliance obligation to do so under this reverted text; whether any state-level or contractual requirement independently preserves that standard is outside this rule's scope. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The NESHAP obligations run to the owner or operator of the rubber tire manufacturing facility, not to carriers, forwarders, or logistics providers moving tires, tire cord, or rubber feedstock. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any workspace activity constitutes "owning or operating" a covered rubber tire manufacturing facility as the subpart defines it; absent that, the workspace sits outside this rule's direct duty-holder class.

# Substantive Requirements

**Reverted existing-source compliance deadline.** The reinstated 2020 Rubber Tire Rule text requires that "if you have an existing affected source, you must comply with the emission limitations for existing sources no later than July 11, 2005," and that an area source that grows into major-source status "must be in compliance with existing source emission limitations no later than 3 years after the date on which the area source became a major source." *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

**Applicability determination.** "You must determine which subpart applies to your source and you must be in compliance with the applicable subpart by the compliance date of that subpart." *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

**Rubber processing subcategory limits removed.** The 2024 Rubber Tire Rule's rubber-processing-subcategory limits, described as the rule's "first-time air emissions standards for the rubber processing subcategory of the rubber tire manufacturing source category," are removed by this action and do not currently bind covered facilities. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

*Specific penalty or enforcement provision not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-12; the captured text addresses the CRA revocation mechanics and the reverted 2020 emission-limitation text, not Clean Air Act enforcement remedies.*

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

The reverted 2020 text carries its own recordkeeping and reporting procedures ("ongoing recordkeeping and reporting procedures in accordance with the general requirements of Sec. 63.10(c), (e)(1), and (e)(2)(i)"), which the owner or operator "shall keep... on record for the life of the affected source or until the affected source is no longer subject to the provisions of this part." *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.* *Specific registration filing format or agency portal not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-12.*

# Operational System Requirements

For workspaces supporting rubber tire or rubber processing manufacturing clients: (1) confirm which subpart and compliance date governs the client's specific affected source now that the 2024 rubber-processing-subcategory standard has been removed, and (2) confirm the client's recordkeeping retention covers the life of the affected source as the reinstated text requires. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.* *Operational implication:* this is a client compliance-posture verification, not a direct system build for the forwarder, since the duty holder is the manufacturing facility. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

# Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- March 5, 2025: U.S. House of Representatives passes H.J. Res. 61 disapproving the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule. In force as of 2026-09-12. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*
- May 6, 2025: U.S. Senate passes H.J. Res. 61. In force as of 2026-09-12. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*
- May 23, 2025: President signs H.J. Res. 61 into law as Public Law 119-14. In force as of 2026-09-12. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*
- November 29, 2024: this final rule's effective date, per the CRA's retroactive-nullification treatment of the disapproved 2024 Rubber Tire Rule ("This final rule is effective November 29, 2024."). In force as of 2026-09-12. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*
- June 22, 2026: EPA publishes this final rule removing the 2024 Rubber Tire Rule's regulatory text. In force as of 2026-09-12. *Source: Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register 2026-12424, June 22 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for.*

# Sources

- Congressional Review Act Revocation of 2024 Amendments to the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Rubber Tire Manufacturing, EPA, Federal Register document 2026-12424, June 22 2026 (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/22/2026-12424/congressional-review-act-revocation-of-2024-amendments-to-the-national-emission-standards-for

# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023, which publishes an updated user's guide setting out the steps organisations need to take to participate in the EU eco-management and audit scheme (EMAS), adopted under Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council. *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.* The Decision "repeal[s]" the prior guide decision: "Article 2 Decision 2013/131/EU is repealed." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

EMAS is established by "Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2009 on the voluntary participation by organisations in a EU eco-management and audit scheme (EMAS)." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.* Participation is voluntary, not a binding compliance obligation. This Decision itself operates at Member State level: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.* *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace, as an organisation potentially seeking EMAS registration for its own environmental management system, would be treated as an "organisation" under Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009 for registration purposes; this Decision's own text does not itself impose an obligation on private operators.

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**COMPETITIVE EDGE.** Assess whether EMAS registration is worth pursuing as a voluntary sustainability credential, since the published guide is intended so that "interested organisations should receive additional information and guidance about the steps needed to participate in EMAS." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.* *Operational implication:* EMAS registration is a differentiator a workspace can cite to clients in cargo verticals with strong environmental scrutiny (e.g., fine art, luxury goods, film and TV logistics), but registration is voluntary and this Decision creates no compliance deadline or penalty exposure for non-participation. *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Decision's addressees are the Member States, who administer EMAS through national competent bodies and environmental verifiers: "the environmental verifier as referred to in Article 2(20) of the EMAS Regulation is... a conformity assessment b[ody]," and organisations may "contact the competent bodies in the countries where the organisations concerned are based." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.* A workspace considering registration would engage its national competent body directly; the workspace is not a duty-holder under this Decision itself.

# Substantive Requirements

**Publication of the guide.** "The user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in Union eco-management and audit scheme as set out in the Annex is hereby published." *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.* The guide's substantive content (environmental review, environmental policy, environmental programme, management system set-up) is voluntary implementation guidance for an organisation pursuing EMAS registration, not a binding requirement imposed by this Decision on external parties.

*Specific compliance deadline, effective date, and penalty provision not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-12: the captured Decision text publishes guidance and repeals a prior guide Decision, and states no entry-into-force clause, no deadline binding external organisations, and no penalty or sanction provision.*

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

Registration under EMAS is voluntary and administered by Member State competent bodies rather than by a jurisdiction-wide filing deadline stated in this Decision. *Specific registration deadline not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-12.*

# Operational System Requirements

For a workspace evaluating EMAS registration: (1) contact the national competent body in the relevant Member State to scope the environmental review, environmental policy, and environmental management system steps the published guide describes, and (2) engage an accredited environmental verifier as defined in Article 2(20) of the EMAS Regulation. *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.* *Operational implication:* these are voluntary program-entry steps, not deadline-bound compliance obligations, so there is no gap-from-baseline analysis of the kind a mandatory regulation would require. *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*

# Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 3 November 2023: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 adopted, repealing Decision 2013/131/EU. In force as of 2026-09-12 (no entry-into-force clause or amendment identified in the captured text). *Source: Commission Decision (EU) 2023/2463 of 3 November 2023 on the publication of the user's guide setting out the steps needed to participate in EMAS, European Commission, OJ L 2023/2463, 10.11.2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023D2463.*
